text: Where you start on an image matters. At a smooth point, the directions you can move in, to first order, form a flat plane as large as the image itself. At the tip of a cone, they don't. <short pause> Zero-initialised LoRA, the usual default, starts exactly at the tip. With B at zero, nudging A changes nothing, so at first only B can move the weights, and fewer directions are open. Split initialisations, which carve a low-rank piece out of the frozen weight, start at a smooth point instead. <short pause> The same lens finds tips where you might not expect them: HRA, a method built from reflections, also starts at one at Hugging Face's default initialisation, when r is even and the frozen weight has full column rank.
